previous_action: Gaius Maximus Valerius makes disciplined training the foundation of his command. He personally trains with the men, teaches them to read terrain and deception, rotates veterans through instruction of less experienced soldiers, and uses repeated field exercises to make obedience to the plan a product of understanding rather than fear. He intends to become the most disciplined man in his command by example, cunning and practice, not by punishments, dismissals or force.

continuity.campaign_development: In July 60 BCE, Valerius made disciplined training the foundation of his command. He personally trained with the men, rotated experienced soldiers through instruction, and used terrain, deception and night exercises to teach soldiers to recognize danger and adapt without relying on fear or arbitrary punishment. A successful mock ambush exercise demonstrated that the command could identify prepared killing ground before entering it. The regional band remains active and the main force remains in the field.
